subject: Clarification: where Helium Health data is processed and how deletion is executed
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@heliumhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Mark Tang <mark.tang@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial questions on where data is processed + deletion timeline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Helium Health is interested in Redwood but we need to confirm some details for our security review. A few concrete questions:

1) Where are user requests executed (regions)? Which cloud regions may see patient-identifiable data for hosted customers?
2) Which subprocessors handle request execution, logs, and backups (names + region footprint)?
3) If a customer requests deletion of a dataset / conversation, what is the end-to-end timeline? What systems still retain data after primary deletion (backups, analytics, traces) and how long?

We’re on a tight procurement window, so a short written summary and any diagrams you have would be helpful.

Best,
Elena
Director of Security, Helium Health

Elena.Park@heliumhealth.com
Helium Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Mark Tang <mark.tang@heliumhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 14:50:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial questions on where data is processed + deletion timeline

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary; attaching a region diagram and our subprocessor inventory for reference. Happy to set up a 30-minute call if you want to walk through any item with our security engineer (cc’d: Marissa).

1) Execution regions (hosted API):
- Primary execution occurs in the region you select at workspace creation. For Helium Health prospects in the EU we typically recommend europe-west1 (GCP) or eu-west-1 (AWS).
- In normal operation, tokens and model inference occur in the chosen runtime region.
- Control-plane operations (billing, model catalog, rollout config) are handled by our control plane and may be processed in our control regions (us-east-1 and europe-west1). Control-plane data does not include raw customer prompts by default; only metadata and usage metrics.

2) Subprocessors and their roles (high-level):
- Compute / model serving: AWS (eu-west-1, us-west-2), Google Cloud (europe-west1, us-central1) — used depending on the customer region and selected model variant.
- Edge / CDN: Cloudflare (global) — for API edge routing and TLS termination.
- Observability & metrics: Datadog (logs/metrics, EU/APAC controls) and Sentry (errors).
- Storage & backups: S3 (AWS) / GCS (GCP) buckets in region; periodic backups may be copied to snapshot storage for durability.
- Secrets & KMS: Customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; we use AWS KMS / GCP KMS in hosted deployments.
- Identity & access: Okta (SaaS customers), internal IAM.
- Analytics / product telemetry: Segment (configurable by account) — telemetry that could include non-PII usage signals; we can opt accounts out.

I attached a detailed spreadsheet listing region footprints for each subprocessor (subprocessor_inventory_20280314.xlsx).

3) Deletion and retention (end-to-end):
- Data types: prompts/responses (conversation payloads), embeddings, request logs, metrics/traces, backups/snapshots.
- Default retention (hosted): conversation payloads: 30 days; embeddings: 90 days; request logs and traces: 30 days; audit logs (billing/usage): 365 days. These are defaults — enterprise customers can request custom retention windows or use Dedicated/Private where retention is under their control.
- Deletion request flow:
  * Customer submits deletion request via Console or API -> ticket created.
  * Primary data deletion: we remove the data from the live store within 72 hours and stop any further processing.
  * Cache/KV purge: KV caches and prefetched prefixes are invalidated within 24 hours; replicated caches within 48 hours.
  * Backups & snapshots: we schedule snapshot purges during the next retention purge cycle; most backups are removed within 30 days (longer for cold-storage snapshots where required by retention policies).
  * Observability/aggregates: we truncate or anonymize any telemetry that references customer identifiers within 30 days; raw logs that contain payloads are rotated out per the logs retention policy and removed within 90 days where applicable.

4) Cross-border notes:
- Processing may cross borders when models are only available in certain clouds or when routing for capacity/latency reasons requires fallback to a compatible region.
- For EU-regulated data we recommend pinning the workspace to an EU-only runtime; in that configuration, we do not route inference outside of EU regions except for control-plane metadata (which contains no raw prompts).
- Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) avoid cross-border transfers entirely — all processing stays under your network boundaries.

Attachments: processing_regions_diagram_v2.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20280314.xlsx

If you want SOC2 / penetration test artifacts, we can share an evidence pack under NDA. I’ll add a short Drive folder (see follow-up).

Best,

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple quick clarifications before we loop procurement/security: 

- On backups: can you confirm whether cold snapshots are encrypted with region-bound keys and whether deletion requests trigger a rekey/purge on those snapshots or only a scheduled purge?
- On logs: do any Datadog/Sentry traces ever contain full prompt/response payloads for hosted customers, or are those redacted before reaching those tools?

If you can answer these two items we’ll put together the risk checklist for our legal team. Mark (cc) will pick up procurement timeline questions.

Best,
Elena
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial questions on where data is processed + deletion timeline

Elena / Mark — quick follow-up answers and next steps:

- Cold snapshots & encryption: yes — snapshots are encrypted at rest using KMS keys scoped to the region. For hosted customers we use provider-managed KMS by default; for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys. Deletion requests do not immediately rekey cold snapshots; instead snapshots containing deleted objects are flagged and purged during the next scheduled snapshot lifecycle (typical max 30 days). If you require immediate key revocation for deleted objects, we can discuss a dedicated retention policy or Private deployment with customer-managed KMS.

- Observability traces & payloads: we do not send full prompt/response payloads to Datadog or Sentry for hosted customers. Error traces include anonymized identifiers and truncated context; by default raw conversational payloads are kept in our regional storage only and are not forwarded to third-party observability tools. For accounts that opt-in to advanced logging, we require explicit config and can route logs to customer-owned storage.

Next steps: I’ve shared a Drive folder with our SOC2 summary and subprocessor inventory (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_evidence). Marissa (cc) is our security lead — she can run a short call with your security team if you want to deep-dive. Do you have availability tomorrow afternoon for a 30-min call?

Regards,
Jonas
